title_en: Does a Judge Incur Sin If He Rules by a Law That Contradicts the Islamic Sharia? | Fatwas of Sheikh al-Dedew
body_ar:
هل يأثم القاضي إذا حكم بقانون مخالف للشريعة الإسلامية؟ | فتاوى الشيخ الددو 

هل ورد مصطلح أهل الحل و العقد في القرآن الكريم أو السنة المطهرة؟

الجواب:

لم يرد مصطلح أهل الحل و العقد في الكتاب و لا السنة، و إنما جاء عن الصحابة الكرام و من بعدهم و اشتهر كثيرا في أيام التابعين و أتباعهم، 

لأن عصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس في حل و لا عقد، لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ولاه الله سبحانه و تعالى أمر المسلمين، و جعله أولى بهم من أنفسهم، و لا يمكن أن ينزع أحد منه الثقة، و لا أن يخالفه [ وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ ۗ وَمَن يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا مُّبِينًا ] [ فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا ] 

و إنما احتيج إلى أهل الحل و العقد بعد وفاته صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث لم يوص بالخلافة لأحد، و لم يعين أحدا لهذا الأمر، فاحتاج المسلمون إلى أن يختاروا منهم أهل الحل و العقد ،

ففي البداية كانت لديهم وسائل واضحة لأن لديهم طائفة زكاها الله في كتابه و رضي عنها فلا تقع سيئاتهم إلا مغفورة، وهم أهل بدر و أهل بيعة الرضوان فقد رضي الله عنه أجمعين، 

و بعد أن مات هؤلاء جميعا احتاج المسلمون إلى معايير يختارون بها أهل الحل و العقد.

فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي
body_en:
[Heading as the CMS carries it:] Does a judge incur sin if he rules by a law that contradicts the Islamic Sharia? | Fatwas of Sheikh al-Dedew

Did the term "the people who bind and loose" (ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd) occur in the Noble Qur'an or in the purified Sunnah?

The answer:

The term "the people who bind and loose" did not occur in the Book, nor in the Sunnah. It came rather from the noble Companions and those after them, and became widely current in the days of the Successors (tābiʿūn) and those who followed them,

because the age of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was not one of binding and loosing: God, glorified and exalted, had given him charge of the affairs of the Muslims and had made him closer to them than their own selves, and no one could withdraw his confidence from him, nor oppose him. { It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has strayed into manifest error } (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:36) { But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them, then find within themselves no discomfort at what you have decided, and submit in full submission } (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:65)

The people who bind and loose were needed only after his death (peace and blessings be upon him), since he did not bequeath the caliphate to anyone and did not designate anyone for this matter, so that the Muslims needed to choose from among themselves the people who bind and loose.

At the outset they had clear means to hand, because they had a group whom God declared upright in His Book and with whom He was pleased, so that no evil deed of theirs falls except that it is forgiven: these were the people of Badr and the people of the Pledge of Ridwan — may God be pleased with them all.

And after all of these had died, the Muslims needed criteria by which to choose the people who bind and loose.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti

flags.note: CRITICAL — TITLE/BODY MISMATCH, the same defect class as record 397. The title asks whether a judge incurs sin by ruling according to a law that contradicts the Sharia. The body never touches that question: it answers whether the term ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd occurs in the Qur'an or Sunnah. A reader arriving at this page in English would take the body as the Sheikh's answer on judges applying secular law, which it is not, and that is a serious misattribution on a politically charged question. critical_for_display is set. Translated faithfully on both sides and flagged; the resolution belongs to the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: لأن لديهم طائفة زكاها الله في كتابه و رضي عنها
options: a group whom God declared upright in His Book
a group whom God pronounced pure in His Book
a group whose integrity God attested in His Book
flags.note: تزكية in this sense is God's attestation of a group's integrity, adjacent to but not identical with the glossary's tazkiyah, 'purification of the self', which is the inward discipline. The glossary entry covers only the tazkiyah sense and does not cover this attestive use.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic (style guide section 4). Surah and verse references were identified by the translator; the source prints the verses without references.

The body opens by repeating the record's own title as a heading before asking a different question; that repetition is part of the served text and has been kept, marked as a heading, so the mismatch is visible rather than hidden.

أهل الحل و العقد is rendered "the people who bind and loose", the established English for those whose agreement constitutes a valid appointment of a ruler. The Arabic is kept in brackets on first occurrence.

The two verses are printed in the source inside square brackets with no references; style guide section 4's curly-brace format and surah references have been applied, and the references were identified by the translator.

Source defect, recorded not fixed: رضي الله عنه أجمعين uses a singular pronoun where the plural عنهم is required. body_ar preserves it; the English renders the evident sense, 'may God be pleased with them all'.
No ruling word appears anywhere in the answer, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged by this text.
